status: AUTHOR ACCEPTED (DECISIONS A9, 2026-10-06): the wind loss factors including the offshore total of about 18.5 % and the solar PR 0.83. The solar_plane_of_array model choices (A13) are PENDING AUTHOR REVIEW.
applies_to: value-corrected profile only (correction p05.vre-loss-factors; decisions Q15 and A1). The doctoral profile applies no factor.
method: Multiplied after the ERA5 -> single-turbine power-curve conversion (wind) or, for solar, after the per-period plane-of-array irradiance of solar_plane_of_array (A13, correction p05.solar-plane-of-array; runs before A13 multiplied the horizontal ssrd/3.6e6 ratio). Per-period shape stays ERA5; curtailment stays a market outcome. There is NO calibration to statistical load factors (Q15, A9).

components.note: Operational wake loss 1.9-6.4 %, mean 4 % (W4); UK onshore farms are smaller, 5 % chosen.
Industry time-based guarantee 97 %; energy-based availability can be lower (Irish case: 11 % energy loss).
Wind-farm annual electrical losses about 2-3 % (W8, excerpt level [E]).
Large offshore farms 10-20 % (W1); European standard farm 8.3 % (W3); 2030 clusters 11-20 % (W2). 12 % chosen for UK clusters.
SPARTA 2017/18 UK portfolio extracted 94.5 % of available wind energy (single source; range not literature).
Offshore absolute value not verified [NV]; the onshore 2-3 % is used as a lower bound (W10 qualitative).

offshore.author_decision: DECISIONS A9 (2026-10-06): the offshore total loss of about 18.5 % is accepted although it exceeds the 'about 10-15 %' of Q15; no statistical calibration.

components.note: UK fleet mean PR 83 % (S1); 84-88 % (S2, S3); France 76 % (S4) as lower bound. PR is defined on plane-of-array irradiance, so under p05.solar-plane-of-array it multiplies the transposed irradiance of solar_plane_of_array (A13); before A13 it multiplied horizontal GHI and missed the tilt gain.

solar_plane_of_array.status: PENDING AUTHOR REVIEW (model choices made under DECISIONS A13; the approach is the author's decision)
solar_plane_of_array.applies_to: value-corrected profile only (correction p05.solar-plane-of-array). The doctoral profile keeps ssrd/3.6e6 on the v1 clock without any factor.

model.tilt: south-facing plane at the Jacobson & Jadhav (2018) annual-optimal tilt for the site latitude
model.geometry: Spencer (1971) declination, equation of time and eccentricity factor; hour angle from local solar time = UTC + longitude/15 h + equation of time; incidence on an equator-facing plane, Duffie & Beckman (2013) eqs 1.6.5 and 1.6.7
model.clock: geometry at the midpoint of every half-hour period of a 365-day UTC model year (period t: day t//48+1, UTC hour (t mod 48)/2 + 0.25); under weather v2 the ERA5 accumulation served to period t is the hour that contains this midpoint (accumulation_end_of_hour: source stamp t//2+1)
model.decomposition: Erbs, Klein & Duffie (1982) hourly diffuse-fraction correlation kd(kt), kt = GHI / (I0n cos z), kt clipped to [0, 1]
model.transposition: Hay & Davies (1980) anisotropic sky: beam x Rb + diffuse x (Ai Rb + (1 - Ai)(1 + cos tilt)/2), Ai = DNI / I0n; ground reflection GHI x albedo x (1 - cos tilt)/2
model.low_sun: zenith above max_zenith_deg or GHI = 0: no beam component, the GHI is treated as isotropic diffuse (so tilt 0 returns GHI exactly)

solar_plane_of_array.tilt_note: Literature optimum fixed tilt for the site latitude, the northern-hemisphere fit of Jacobson & Jadhav (2018): tilt = 1.3793 + lat (1.2011 + lat (-0.014404 + lat 0.000080509)) degrees, about 35.7-37.7 degrees for the GBP1 representative sites (50.7-56.0 N). A13 allows the site latitude instead (textbook rule, P3); on GBP1 it is steeper than the optimum for the diffuse-rich UK climate and gives a smaller gain (sensitivity reported in the methodology draft).
solar_plane_of_array.disclosure: GBP1 weather is an ERA5 2020-2024 average climatology (finding P6-09): averaging smooths the hourly clearness index, so the decomposition gives a larger diffuse share and a smaller tilt gain than single-year hourly data would. The resulting capacity factors are reported next to DUKES 6.3 (A9, A13); they are not calibrated.
